report.source_text: Therefore, the patient at age of 12 months undergoes cross-union surgery, with evidence of good healing progress (Fig. 6).

clinician.trajectory_summary: Newborn presented with severe respiratory distress and subsequent inconsolable crying and reduced mobility in the left lower limb. Initial imaging (X-ray) identified a mid-diaphyseal tibial fracture without history of trauma. Follow-up imaging over 2 to 8 months showed absent osseous consolidation (non-union), cortical discontinuity, bone thickening, hypodense areas in tibia, and fibula bowing, consistent with congenital pseudarthrosis. At 12 months, the patient underwent successful cross-union surgery with good healing progress, confirming the diagnosis and effective management.
